projects.title: Where Champions Are Made

card.alt: A University of Washington athletics building entrance with a large W sign and yellow sport words painted on the ground

hero.alt: A University of Washington athletics building entrance with a large W sign and yellow sport words painted on the ground

projects.summary:
For three years I trained in UW Athletics' facilities and wondered what they would feel like if they reflected the same pride, identity and passion we competed with. This capstone reimagines the department's brand experience through pictograms, signage and spatial graphics.

The system pairs custom sport pictograms and arena maps with large-scale storytelling walls, so athletes, staff and visitors can find their way while honoring the Olympians, national champions and All-Americans who define the program's legacy.

sections.heading: Challenge
sections.body: University of Washington's athletic facilities lacked cohesive wayfinding and spatial identity. Despite serving Olympic-level and D1 athletes, the environment felt disconnected and difficult to navigate. As both a designer and D1 athlete who trained in these spaces daily, I recognized the gap between the caliber of athletes and the quality of their environment.

sections.heading: Solution
sections.body: Designed a comprehensive wayfinding and environmental graphics system including custom pictograms, modular signage architecture, spatial storytelling installations, and user journey mapping for three distinct audiences (athletes, staff, visitors). The system balances athletic identity with functional clarity.

sections.heading: Impact
sections.body: System establishes visual consistency across 50+ facility touchpoints, improves navigation clarity for 800+ student athletes, and transforms underutilized spaces into branded environments that reinforce UW Athletics' competitive identity.

projects.title: Share a Smile

card.alt: A scatter of colorful Share a Smile cards

projects.summary:
Extended brand graphics, creative direction and select photography for Share a Smile, Tyler Artis's campaign and social club built around the smile as a form of connection.

The design direction intended to invite people in while leaving room for the complexity behind a smile. I drew inspiration from honest storytelling, with bright colors, fun photography and expressive typography, while staying true to Tyler's original logo.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: Share a Smile is a visual campaign and social club built around one idea: joy as a form of connection. The work leans on honest storytelling and expressive design, with soft textures, bold type and community touchpoints that treat the smile as something powerful and real.

sections.heading: The brief
sections.body: Tyler came in with the idea that a smile could change someone's day. Together we pushed it further: what if a smile could be a form of connection, defiance or healing? The goal was never just to make something look good. It was to build a story around a radical kind of optimism.

sections.heading: My role
sections.body: Tyler Artis created the Share a Smile logo and owns the brand. My part is the supporting brand world around it: extended brand graphics, creative direction and select photography, developed as an ongoing collaboration since 2022.

original.brief_paragraph_shown_until_2026-10-25: When I was brought on to design for the Share a Smile Project, the goal wasn’t just to make something visually appealing—it was to help build a narrative around a radical kind of optimism. The client came in with the idea that a smile could change someone’s day, and together we pushed that further: what if a smile could be a form of connection, defiance, or healing?
original.role_paragraph_shown_until_2026-10-25: As the lead designer, I worked to translate that ethos into a visual system and story that felt honest, empathetic, and active. We weren’t interested in empty feel-good messages. Instead, we treated the phrase as a design element with power... something that could travel across print, space, and community. I helped develop everything from the campaign’s tone of voice to the layout of story-collecting booths and print collateral. We used bright colors, fun photography and expressive typography to invite people in, while still making room for the complexity behind the act of smiling. It was about seeing people, really seeing them, and acknowledging that sometimes joy is an act of resistance. The final identity reflected that spirit: approachable, unexpected, and a little bit brave.
original.credit_confirmed_2026-10-25: Tyler Artis created the original logo and owns the brand. Prestin's contributions: extended brand graphics, creative direction, select photography. Ongoing.

projects.title: Black Irons Golf

card.alt: The Black Irons Golf Group mark over a black-and-white photo of a golfer

hero.alt: Golfers beside a giant sand trap, captioned: there's a lesson in every green

projects.summary:
For Black Irons Golf Group, a brand built for Black golfers, I wanted the identity to feel rooted in culture, community and self-expression, and bold enough to challenge who the game is for.

Instead of a standard golf crest, I drew the mark from the game itself: a Sankofa bird, the symbol of learning from the past to build the future.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: Black Irons Golf Group is a brand built for Black golfers, rooted in culture, community, and self-expression. The identity blends sharp detailing and elegant restraint to challenge who the game is for and redefine what belonging looks like—on and off the course.

sections.heading: The mark
sections.body: The symbol of the bird (Sankofa) highlighting the importance of learning from the past to build the future. Head of the bird is in the shape of a 9 iron. Neck of the body is in the shape of a golf swing. Feathers of the bird reflect the splay that comes from hitting in sand traps or on the fairway.

projects.title: Partners in Print

card.alt: An overhead render of the BE BOLD exhibition space

projects.summary:
Partners in Print, a Seattle nonprofit, was moving into a new home in Belltown. After pitching their revitalization, our team imagined how its exterior and interior could come to life for the grand opening.

BE BOLD reimagines letterpress as something big, physical and performative: a fictional steamroller and oversized floor prints turn the printing process into a spectacle.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: With a Seattle-based nonprofit organization moving into a new space, we conceptualized how the exterior and interior could come to life for their grand opening. BE BOLD is an exhibition concept for Partners in Print that reimagines letterpress as bold, physical, and performative. It is centered around a fictional steamroller and oversized floor prints that turn process into spectacle.

projects.title: Rapport

card.alt: A line drawing of the Rapport storefront

hero.alt: A line drawing of the Rapport storefront on textured paper

projects.summary:
Rapport is a self-pour wine and beer bar on Seattle's Capitol Hill, inspired by the art of conversation. The identity invites guests to slow down, share a moment and explore at their own pace.

Two patterns carry the brand: wine glasses that twist like grape vines, and beer glasses stacked like brick, a nod to the neighborhood. High-flash photography, with its hard shadow, echoes the logo's bold border.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: Rapport is a self-pour wine bar rooted in hospitality and connection. Inspired by the Pacific Northwest and built around community, the identity invites guests to slow down, share moments, and explore wine on their own terms.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body: The history of self-pour wine bars reflects a convergence of technological innovation, changing consumer preferences, and a desire for more interactive and immersive drinking experiences. Rapport reflects a relatively young history dating back to a recent 2020. However being such a young restaurant, and a staple in the Seattle area, Rapport has the opportunity to take risks, and be unconventional and daring in their identity.

sections.heading: Patterns
sections.body: The repeated wine glass pattern is shaped to reflect grape vines and create the complex look of the vines. The repeated beer glass pattern is shaped to reflect bricks as a nod to the Capitol Hill area where the store is located.

sections.heading: Photography
sections.body: Photos of people should have a unique look. This can be done with a simple point and shoot camera using flash. This look is known as high flash. The style of this is chosen because of the dark shadow that falls out the back of the photo, mimicking the bold border line in the logo. When using photos of places or things for adverts, a color filter should be applied. Adding a core supporting color over the photo allows the viewer to see the photo but also reestablishes the brand colors.

projects.title: Loosely
projects.summary:
Loosely is a concert companion app concept designed to make planning a night out with friends feel like part of the experience. Between meeting up, finding your seats, and keeping everyone on the same page, there's a lot to coordinate before the music even starts.

The app brings everything together through shared plans, personalized itineraries, and navigation through a paired watch. I wanted to make the moments leading up to a concert feel just as exciting as the show itself.

sections.heading: Project introduction
sections.body:
Going to a concert with friends means more than just showing up for the music. Between making plans, finding your seats, and keeping everyone on the same page, there's a whole night to coordinate.

Loosely is a concert companion app concept that brings those plans together through personalized itineraries, shared reminders, and navigation. I wanted to make the anticipation and preparation feel just as much a part of the experience as the concert itself.

sections.heading: Seat navigation
sections.body: Paired with a watch, Loosely provides real-time directions from your current location to your next destination, including your seat inside the venue.

sections.heading: Keeping everyone in sync
sections.body: As each part of the itinerary approaches, the group receives a reminder and can follow the map to wherever they're headed next.

original.cargo:
Loosely — UI/UX app design

Problem: Concerts demand the same kind of coordination as a team event, but fans are left to figure it out on their own.
Solution:
Loosely is a concert companion app that centralizes planning, personalizes the itinerary, and brings the group together before the night even starts.

The design goal: Make preparation feel like part of the experience.

Seat navigation

With a paired watch, you can get to your next location or even your venue seats at the concert with real-time directions based on your current location.

Know what's next and where to go

When the time reaches a new event time slot, the group will get a notification and can navigate to the place with the map
